interpretations: "At least one lab record with both U-PRO and RA equal to '-'" means a single lab record (same row/date) where U-PRO = '-' and RA = '-' simultaneously. Averages are then computed across all of that patient's lab records, including records where the condition doesn't hold.
The condition is met if the patient has some record with U-PRO = '-' and some record (possibly a different date) with RA = '-'. The two conditions are not required to hold on the same row.
The averages are computed only over the lab records where both U-PRO and RA are '-', not across all of the patient's records.

"Average ALP and average HCT" are the plain AVG over non-null values, computed separately for each column. ALP and HCT may each be averaged over a different number of rows, because nulls are ignored per column.
The averages are computed only over rows where both ALP and HCT are non-null, so the two averages use the same rows.
Patients are limited to those who appear in the Patient table (inner join). Lab records with no matching Patient row are excluded.
Patients with no Patient row are kept with a null sex. This contradicts the question's "only patients present there", so it is unlikely.
Sorting by average HCT descending places null averages last. This is done either with an explicit null-last ordering or by relying on a database default that happens to put nulls last.
Ties in average HCT are broken arbitrarily, by patient ID ascending, or by another unspecified rule. Which 10 patients appear then varies.
"Top 10" is a LIMIT 10 on the sorted result, giving at most 10 rows.
"Top 10" includes ties at the 10th position, so more than 10 rows could be returned.
'-' is matched as the literal string '-'. Values like '+-' or '-' with whitespace are not counted.
'-' is treated as a normal/negative marker that could include '+-' (the documentation lists normal as '-' or '+-'). The question says '-' only, so this is unlikely.
The output is one row per patient, with columns ID, SEX, avg ALP and avg HCT. The averages are unrounded.
